title: Cassowary baited camera trap observations in Paluma 2023-2024
description: This camera trap survey was carried out to examine the population of cassowaries (Casuarius casuarius) in Paluma Range National Park. This was acheived by sampling many areas throughout the park and using colored lures (painted red and blue balls) that increase the likelihood of detecting cassowaries. Paluma National Park is the southern extent of the cassowaries range and little is known about their populations in this area. As this area is isolated from the rest of the Wet Tropics by sclerophyll forest is it important to understand if there are corridors the cassowaries are using to travel between fragments, or of this population is completely isolated

schema.name: deployments
schema.title: Deployments
schema.description: Table with camera trap placements (deployments). Includes `deploymentID`, start, end, location and camera setup information.

fields.name: deploymentID
fields.description: Unique identifier of the deployment.

fields.name: locationID
fields.description: Identifier of the deployment location.

fields.name: locationName
fields.description: Name given to the deployment location. Some location names from the CAPAD dataset were overwritten from Girringun_IPA to Paluma_Range_NP to maintain consistency due to close proximity. This is denoted by the column CAPADlocationName in the WildObs verified spatial hierarchy.

fields.name: latitude
fields.description: Latitude of the deployment location in decimal degrees, using the WGS84 datum.

fields.name: longitude
fields.description: Longitude of the deployment location in decimal degrees, using the WGS84 datum.

fields.name: coordinateUncertainty
fields.description: Horizontal distance from the given `latitude` and `longitude` describing the smallest circle containing the deployment location. Expressed in meters. Especially relevant when coordinates are rounded to protect sensitive species.

fields.name: deploymentStart
fields.description: Date and time at which the deployment was started. Formatted as an ISO 8601 string with timezone designator (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ` or `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss±hh:mm`).

fields.name: deploymentEnd
fields.description: Date and time at which the deployment was ended. Formatted as an ISO 8601 string with timezone designator (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ` or `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss±hh:mm`).

fields.name: setupBy
fields.description: Name or identifier of the person or organization that deployed the camera.

fields.name: cameraID
fields.description: Identifier of the camera used for the deployment (e.g. the camera device serial number).

fields.name: cameraModel
fields.description: Manufacturer and model of the camera. Formatted as `manufacturer-model`.

fields.name: cameraDelay
fields.description: Predefined duration after detection when further activity is ignored. Expressed in seconds.

fields.name: cameraHeight
fields.description: Height at which the camera was deployed. Expressed in meters. Not to be combined with `cameraDepth`.

fields.name: cameraDepth
fields.description: Depth at which the camera was deployed. Expressed in meters. Not to be combined with `cameraHeight`.

fields.name: cameraTilt
fields.description: Angle at which the camera was deployed in the vertical plane. Expressed in degrees, with `-90` facing down, `0` horizontal and `90` facing up.

fields.name: cameraHeading
fields.description: Angle at which the camera was deployed in the horizontal plane. Expressed in decimal degrees clockwise from north, with values ranging from `0` to `360`: `0` = north, `90` = east, `180` = south, `270` = west.

fields.name: detectionDistance
fields.description: Maximum distance at which the camera can reliably detect activity. Expressed in meters. Typically measured by having a human move in front of the camera.

fields.name: timestampIssues
fields.description: `true` if timestamps in the `media` resource for the deployment are known to have (unsolvable) issues (e.g. unknown timezone, am/pm switch).

fields.name: baitUse
fields.description: `true` if bait was used for the deployment. More information can be provided in `tags` or `comments`.

fields.name: featureType
fields.description: Type of the feature (if any) associated with the deployment.

fields.name: habitat
fields.description: Short characterization of the habitat at the deployment location.

fields.name: deploymentGroups
fields.description:
Deployment group(s) associated with the deployment. Deployment groups can have a spatial (arrays, grids, clusters), temporal (sessions, seasons, months, years) or other context. Formatted as a pipe (`|`) separated list for multiple values, with values preferably formatted as `key:value` pairs. 

 In this data, deploymentGroups have been spatially defined to occur within a single locationName, which is assumed to be spatially distinct. DeploymentGroups have been made temporally distinct using a maximum duration of 100 days.

fields.name: deploymentTags
fields.description: Tag(s) associated with the deployment. Formatted as a pipe (`|`) separated list for multiple values, with values optionally formatted as `key:value` pairs.

fields.name: deploymentComments
fields.description: Comments or notes about the deployment.

fields.name: multiSeason_deploymentGroup
fields.description: Long-term sampling based on spatially and temporally limited deploymentGroups. Continuous sampling was split into new multiSeason_deploymentGroups using a cutoff time of 30 days between deploymentGroups. This is the parent column to deploymentGroups, where multiple deploymentGroups may be nested within a single multiSeason_deploymentGroup value.

fields.name: projectName
fields.description: This is the persistent identifier used to describe the overall datapackage, stored in dataPackage$id. This identifier is used to manage and track many different dataPackages. This value is a short url-usable and preferably human-readable name of the package. The name should be invariant, meaning that it should not change when a data package is updated.

schema.name: observations
schema.title: Observations
schema.description: Table with observations derived from the media files. Associated with deployments (`deploymentID`). Observations can mark non-animal events (camera setup, human, blank) or one or more animal observations (`observationType` = `animal`) of a certain taxon, count, life stage, sex, behavior and/or individual. Observations can be made at different levels (`observationLevel`).

fields.name: observationID
fields.description: Unique identifier of the observation, as defined by a temporal interval of 5 minutes. This is the smallest value in the hierarchy of temporal organization. ObservationID serves as the primary key for the observations table (i.e., one unique value per row)

fields.name: deploymentID
fields.description: Identifier of the deployment the observation belongs to. Foreign key to `deployments.deploymentID`.

fields.name: mediaID
fields.description: Identifier of the media file that was classified. Only applicable for media-based observations (`observationLevel` = `media`). Foreign key to `media.mediaID`.

fields.name: eventID
fields.description: Unique identifier of the event, as defined by a temporal interval of 30 minutes. This is the highest value in the hierarchy of temporal organization. There can be multiple different observationIDs nested within a single eventID.

fields.name: eventStart
fields.description: Date and time at which the first media file comprising an observationID was captured. Defined by a temporal interval of 5 minutes. Formatted as an ISO 8601 string with timezone designator (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ` or `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss±hh:mm`).

fields.name: eventEnd
fields.description: Date and time at which the last media file comprising an observationID was captured.  Defined by a temporal interval of 5 minutes. Formatted as an ISO 8601 string with timezone designator (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ` or `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss±hh:mm`).

fields.name: observationLevel
fields.description: Level at which the observation was classified. `media` for media-based observations that are directly associated with a media file (`mediaID`). These are especially useful for machine learning and don't need to be mutually exclusive (e.g. multiple classifications are allowed). `event` for event-based observations that consider an event (comprising a collection of media files). These are especially useful for ecological research and should be mutually exclusive, so that their `count` can be summed.

fields.name: observationType
fields.description: Type of the observation. All categories in this vocabulary have to be understandable from an AI point of view. `unknown` describes classifications with a `classificationProbability` below some predefined threshold i.e. neither humans nor AI can say what was recorded.

fields.name: cameraSetupType
fields.description: Type of the camera setup action (if any) associated with the observation.

fields.name: scientificName
fields.description: Scientific name of the observed individual(s).

fields.name: count
fields.description: Number of observed individuals (optionally of given life stage, sex and behavior).

fields.name: lifeStage
fields.description: Age class or life stage of the observed individual(s).

fields.name: sex
fields.description: Sex of the observed individual(s)

fields.name: behavior
fields.description: Dominant behavior of the observed individual(s), preferably expressed as controlled values (e.g. grazing, browsing, rooting, vigilance, running, walking). Formatted as a pipe (`|`) separated list for multiple values, with the dominant behavior listed first.

fields.name: individualID
fields.description: Identifier of the observed individual.

fields.name: individualPositionRadius
fields.description: Distance from the camera to the observed individual identified by `individualID`. Expressed in meters. Required for distance analyses (e.g. [Howe et al. 2017](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.12790)) and random encounter modelling (e.g. [Rowcliffe et al. 2011](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2041-210X.2011.00094.x)).

fields.name: individualPositionAngle
fields.description: Angular distance from the camera view centerline to the observed individual identified by `individualID`. Expressed in degrees, with negative values left, `0` straight ahead and positive values right. Required for distance analyses (e.g. [Howe et al. 2017](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.12790)) and random encounter modelling (e.g. [Rowcliffe et al. 2011](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2041-210X.2011.00094.x)).

fields.name: individualSpeed
fields.description: Average movement speed of the observed individual identified by `individualID`. Expressed in meters per second. Required for random encounter modelling (e.g. [Rowcliffe et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1002/rse2.17)).

fields.name: bboxX
fields.description: Horizontal position of the top-left corner of a bounding box that encompasses the observed individual(s) in the media file identified by `mediaID`. Or the horizontal position of an object in that media file. Measured from the left and relative to media file width.

fields.name: bboxY
fields.description: Vertical position of the top-left corner of a bounding box that encompasses the observed individual(s) in the media file identified by `mediaID`. Or the vertical position of an object in that media file. Measured from the top and relative to the media file height.

fields.name: bboxWidth
fields.description: Width of a bounding box that encompasses the observed individual(s) in the media file identified by `mediaID`. Measured from the left of the bounding box and relative to the media file width.

fields.name: bboxHeight
fields.description: Height of the bounding box that encompasses the observed individual(s) in the media file identified by `mediaID`. Measured from the top of the bounding box and relative to the media file height.

fields.name: classificationMethod
fields.description: Method (most recently) used to classify the observation.

fields.name: classifiedBy
fields.description: Name or identifier of the person or AI algorithm that (most recently) classified the observation.

fields.name: classificationTimestamp
fields.description: Date and time of the (most recent) classification. Formatted as an ISO 8601 string with timezone designator (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ` or `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss±hh:mm`).

fields.name: classificationProbability
fields.description: Degree of certainty of the (most recent) classification. Expressed as a probability, with `1` being maximum certainty. Omit or provide an approximate probability for human classifications.

fields.name: observationTags
fields.description: Tag(s) associated with the observation. Formatted as a pipe (`|`) separated list for multiple values, with values optionally formatted as `key:value` pairs.

fields.name: observationComments
fields.description: Comments or notes about the observation.

fields.description: The amount of time, in seconds, between distinct eventIDs

fields.name: ecoregion_intactness_point
fields.description: The Ecoregion Intactness Index (ecoregion_intactness) values calcuated with a meter buffer around each deploymentID. This index is a simplistic binary characterisation of habitat and non-habitat with a focus on change in habitat extent has dominated conservation assessments across different spatial scales. This metric captures both habitat loss, quality and fragmentation effects and is calculated using continuous measures of habitat quality. The index is applied at a global scale to quantify changes in intactness of the world's terrestrial ecoregions over a 16 year period. This variable has been calculated with a 1 meter buffer around each deploymentID.

source.citation: Beyer, H.L., Venter, O., Grantham, H.S. & Watson, J.E.M. (2019) Substantial losses in ecoregion intactness highlights urgency of globally coordinated action. Conservation Letters. Volume 13, Issue 2

fields.name: GEEBAM_fire_severity_2020_point
fields.description: Dominant fire severity class for each location based on the Australian Google Earth Engine Burnt Area Map (AUS GEEBAM), produced after the 2019/20 bushfire season. Values represent the most frequently occurring fire severity class (mode) within the buffer area surrounding each camera deployment. A score of 0 means unburnt, 1 = very low burn, 2 = low burn, 3 = moderate burn, 4 = high burn, 5 = very high/extreme burn. The AUS GEEBAM dataset was developed using Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and represents fire severity across the National Indicative Aggregated Fire Extent Dataset (NIAFED) as of 25 February 2020. Values are derived from a categorical classification and not continuous metrics. This variable has been calculated with a buffer around each deploymentID. This variable has been calculated with a 1 meter buffer around each deploymentID.

Values represent the percentage of area per each fire severity classification within a  buffer around each deploymentID. Across the 5 fire severity percentage columns, each coordinate totals to 100%. A fire severity of 1 = very low burn, 2 = low burn, 3 = moderate burn, 4 = high burn, 5 = very high/extreme burn. The AUS GEEBAM dataset was developed using Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and represents fire severity across the National Indicative Aggregated Fire Extent Dataset (NIAFED) as of 25 February 2020. Values are derived from a categorical classification and not continuous metrics. This variable has been calculated with a NA meter buffer around each deploymentID.

fields.name: fire_events_count_point
fields.description: Count of historical fire events intersecting a buffer around each camera deployment location. Fire events are derived from the combined Australian Fire Boundaries dataset, which integrates Geoscience Australia's Historical Bushfire Boundaries (Version 2.0, covering 1899-2023) and Near Real-Time Bushfire Boundaries (covering 2025-present). Each fire polygon represents either a bushfire or prescribed burn boundary as mapped by state/territory fire management agencies. The count includes all fires (both bushfires and prescribed burns) whose boundaries intersect the buffer area, regardless of fire size or date. Note: Northern Territory fires are not included in the historical dataset, and 2024 data is unavailable due to a gap between datasets. This variable has been calculated with a buffer around each deploymentID. This variable has been calculated with a 1 meter buffer around each deploymentID.

source.citation: Foo, A., Coghlan, R., Orr, K. (2023). Historical Bushfire Boundaries - Version 2.0. Commonwealth of Australia (Geoscience Australia). https://doi.org/10.26186/149017; Geoscience Australia (2025). Near Real-Time Bushfire Boundaries. Commonwealth of Australia.

fields.name: HCAS_static_point
fields.description: This variable represents the long-term (1988-2022) estimate of habitat condition across Australia, derived from the Habitat Condition Assessment System (HCAS v3.1). Condition values are calculated using a nationally consistent ecological model that incorporates vegetation structure, land use, connectivity, and degradation pressure, and are scaled from 0 to 1, where 1 = very high integrity and 0 = very low integrity. This variable has been calculated with a buffer around each deploymentID. This variable has been calculated with a 1 meter buffer around each deploymentID.

fields.name: Olson_global_ecoregion
fields.description: Categorical variable identifying the terrestrial ecoregion in which a camera deployment falls. Ecoregions are large geographic units of land that share similar climate, ecological communities, and environmental conditions, as defined in Terrestrial Ecoregions of the World: A New Map of Life on Earth (Olson et al., 2001). Each ecoregion is part of a biome and realm, and has a unique name and numeric code. The classification includes 867 terrestrial ecoregions, covering the globe. This variable has been calculated with a buffer around each deploymentID. This variable has been calculated with a 1 meter buffer around each deploymentID.
example: Biome: 1, name: Queensland tropical rain forests

fields.name: standardized_precipitation_index_point
fields.description: The Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI-12), a unitless z-score representing the precipitation anomaly over the preceding 12 months, calculated with a buffer around each deploymentID. Values are derived from the CHIRPS v2.0 dataset, which provides quasi-global 0.05 degree (~5 km) gridded precipitation estimates from 1981 to near-present. Positive SPI values indicate wetter-than-normal conditions, negative values indicate drier-than-normal conditions, and values near zero indicate average conditions. This variable has been calculated with a 1 meter buffer around each deploymentID.

fields.name: HIF_point
fields.description: Human Industrial Footprint (HIF) index value representing cumulative human industrial pressure on the landscape, extracted from a 100 m resolution raster mapped in Albers Equal Area projection (EPSG:3577). The HIF was computed by summing 16 nationally relevant scored pressure layers (each scaled 0-10), including intensive land uses, buildings, mining, human population density, croplands, pasturelands, forestry plantations, reservoirs, farm dams, roads, railways, energy transmission lines, oil pipelines, gas pipelines, hiking trails, and navigable waterways. Higher values indicate greater industrial pressure. This variable has been calculated with a 1 meter buffer around each deploymentID.

fields.name: EII_point
fields.description: Ecological Intactness Index (EII) value representing the degree of ecological intactness of the surrounding landscape, extracted from a 100 m resolution raster mapped in Albers Equal Area projection (EPSG:3577). The EII is derived from the Human Industrial Footprint (HIF) and is parameterised to be proportional to habitat area when there is no fragmentation, to decline monotonically as fragmentation increases (sensitive to both the number of nearby patches and separation between patches), and to be proportional to habitat quality for a given total habitat area and degree of fragmentation. Values range from 0 (no intactness) to 1 (fully intact). This variable has been calculated with a 1 meter buffer around each deploymentID.

fields.name: IBRAsubRegionName
fields.description: Categorical variable representing the Interim Biogeographic Regionalisation for Australia (IBRA) Bioregion in which a location falls. Bioregions are large, ecologically distinct areas based on climate, geology, landform, native vegetation, and species distribution. Australia is divided into 89 IBRA bioregions, which form the foundation for biodiversity planning and reporting. This variable is from Version 7. This variable has been calculated with a 1 meter buffer around each deploymentID. Each of the 89 IBRA bioregions is further divided into 419 subregions representing more refined ecological characteristics. This variable has been calculated with a 1 meter buffer around each deploymentID.

source.citation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW). (2020). Interim Biogeographic Regionalisation for Australia (IBRA), Version 7 (Subregions). Australian Government.
